ITQAN:v3p266/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.claim: The Qur'an favors the rarer of synonyms, such as ضيزى, الحطمة, سقر, لظى, and هاوية, often to preserve each surah's rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.anchor: إيثار أغرب اللفظتين نحو ﴿ قسمة ضيزى ﴾ ولم يقل ( جائرة )

BURSEVI:v10p386/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r4.claim: Hawiya names Hell because of its extreme depth; a report says its inhabitants fall through it for seventy years.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r4.anchor: هي من أسماء النار سميت بها لغاية عمقها وبعدها مهواها روى أن أهل النار يهوى فيها سبعين خريفا

BURSEVI:v10p386/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p386/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi describes Hawiya as the lowest of all the gates of Hell.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r5.anchor: وآن دركه باشذد زير ترين همه دركها

BURSEVI:v10p386/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r6.claim: “Mother” means their refuge, as a child seeks its mother; it can also be taunting, enclose them like a womb, or mark the origin to which a fire-created unbeliever returns; the author says this last explanation is apparent.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r6.anchor: وعبر عن المأوى بالأم لأن أهلها يأوون إليها كما يأوى الولد إلى أمه

BURSEVI:v10p386/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r7.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p386/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf relates the curse “his mother fell,” since the person's fall and death make his mother collapse in grief.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r7.anchor: من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة هوت أمه لأنه إذا هوى أي سقط وهلك

BURSEVI:v10p386/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r8.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v10p386/r8.claim: Qatada says the person's head is cast into Hell as its “mother”; umm al-ra’s means either the brain or its thin covering.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r8.anchor: وعن قتادة فأم رأسه هاوية في جهنم لأنه يطرح فيها منكوسا

BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.claim: The inward reading makes the origin of those with light scales an abyss of veiling and a hot fire of ignorance, blindness, ego, passion, Satan, and the world.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.anchor: فأصله المجبول عليه هاوية الحجاب من الأزل إلى الأبد وهي نار حامية بنار الجهل والعمى

BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.claim: Both groups commit sins, though the first has fewer and outweighed sins and the second has many; the trial remains, so the Prophet tells ‘Ali to follow a bad deed with a good one, in keeping with God's forgiving name.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.anchor: لعلي رضي الله عنه يا علي إذا عملت سيئة فاعمل بجنبها حسنة

BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.claim: God's scale reverses ordinary scales: rising and elevation are heaviness, while falling is lightness; weighty deeds are enduring good works, and valueless light deeds are passing sensual pleasures.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.anchor: اعلم أن ميزان الحق بخلاف ميزان الخلق إذ صعود الموزونات وارتفاعها فيه هو الثقل

BURSEVI:v10p386/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r12.claim: In the inward reading, Hawiya is the abyss of corporeal nature; the things truly weighed are primordial hidden capacities and intellectual receptivities, set as right- and left-hand pans.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r12.anchor: وفي الهاوية إشارة إلى هاوية الطبيعة الجسمانية التي يهوى فيها أهلها

QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.claim: Light scales are evil deeds and psychic vices; their owner’s home is the abyss of bodily nature’s hell.
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.anchor: بأن كانت من الأعمال السيئة والرذائل النفسانية { فأمه هاوية }

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.claim: Those whose evil deeds have no weight face eternal Hell; any good deeds are nullified by ill intent and heretical belief, and the next verse identifies the abyss as blazing fire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.anchor: due to their ill-int entions and heretical beliefs.

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.claim: Those whose scales are light in acts of obedience are the disbelievers, whose abode is the abyss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r4.claim: Hāwiya is a level of Hell; umm means a place of refuge or dwelling, just as earth is called humanity's mother.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r4.anchor: فأمه هاوية: الهاوية دركة من دركات النار، وأمه معناه مأواه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r5.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r5.claim: Qatada, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and others say the person's head is his destination and will be thrown headfirst to the bottom of Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح وغيره: فأم رأسه هاوية في قعر جهنم لأنه يطرح فيها منكوسا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r6.claim: Another view hears an ill omen: when people curse someone with his mother's ruin, they imagine her falling into grief when he falls and dies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو تفاؤل بشر، وإذا دعوا بالهلكة قالوا هوت أمه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r7.claim: The majority pronounce the hamza of ummuhu with ḍamma; Ṭalḥa uses kasra, which Ibn Khalawayh cites as a dialect but grammarians restrict after a preceding kasra or yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فأمه بضم الهمزة، وطلحة بكسرها.

FARRA:v3p286/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p286/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p286/r6.claim: His mother is made his refuge, as a woman shelters her child, because he has no other refuge.
FARRA:v3p286/r6.anchor: وقوله جل وعز: فأمه هاوية (9) . صارت مأواه، كما تؤوي المرأة ابنها، فجعلها إذ لا مأوى له غيرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r2.claim: His abode is the Fire; it is called a mother because people naturally find their resting place with their mothers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r2.anchor: مسكنه النار، سمي المسكن أما لأن الأصل في السكون إلى الأمهات،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r3.claim: Al-Hawiya is a name for Hell and means a chasm whose bottom cannot be reached.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r3.anchor: والهاوية اسم من أسماء جهنم، وهو المهواة لا يدرك قعرها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r4.claim: Qatada says Arabs use hawat ummuhu of someone who has fallen into a grave predicament.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: وهي كلمة عربية تقولها العرب للرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r5.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes ummuhu as his head: they plunge into the Fire headfirst, upside down.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r5.anchor: وقيل: ["فأمه هاوية"] أراد أم رأسه ["منحدرة منكوسة"] يعني أنهم يهوون في النار على رءوسهم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r7.claim: Hāwiya is Hell, the person’s abode and a name for the destructive abyss; the answer to ‘what is it?’ is a blazing fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r7.anchor: { فأمه هاوية } فمأواه النار المحرقة والهاوية من أسمائها ولذلك قال: { وما أدراك ما هيه نار حامية }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.claim: Light scales mean evil deeds prevail or the person has no good deed because they followed falsehood; their refuge is the Hawiya, a very low, fiery abyss.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.anchor: بأن غلبت سيئاته أو لم تكن له حسنة لاتباعه الباطل وخفته عليه في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.claim: Hawiya is a sheltering abode, like a mother or the earth one returns to; the sinner continually falls through its depths, and the omitted clauses form an antithetical ellipsis.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.anchor: أي التي تؤويه وتضمه إليها كما يقال للأرض : أم

NAHHAS:v5p280/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r11.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v5p280/r11.claim: He says the person's mother is his settled place and interprets hāwiya as the Fire; he cites a poet's line about a fallen mother.
NAHHAS:v5p280/r11.anchor:
وهاوية نار وأنشد
( هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح غاديا

NAHHAS:v5p280/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r12.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p280/r12.claim: Another view takes umm as the origin or core of something, so the person is doomed; ‘mother of the Qurʾān’ and a poem about earth's mother support this sense.
NAHHAS:v5p280/r12.anchor: أصله هاو أي هالك لأن أم الشيء أصله

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r8.claim: Qatada explains hawiyah as the Fire to which a person’s fate leads.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأمه هاوية} قال: مصيره إلى النار وهي الهاوية

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reads fa-ummuhu hawiyah as the idiom “his mother has fallen.”
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فأمه هاوية} كقولك هويت أمه

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r10.claim: Qatada says Arabs use “his mother has fallen” for someone caught in a terrible affair.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r10.anchor: عن قتادة قال: هي كلمة عربية إذا وقع رجل في أمر شديد قالوا: هويت أمه

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r11.speaker: أبو خالد الوالبي
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r11.claim: Abu Khalid al-Walibi interprets “his mother” as the top of his head.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r11.anchor: عن أبي خالد الوالبي {فأمه هاوية} قال: أم رأسه

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r12.claim: Ikrima says the top of the sinner’s head falls into Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r12.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: أم رأسه هاوية في جهنم

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r13.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r13.claim: Abu Salih says they fall into the Fire headfirst.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r13.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال: يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says hawiyah is the Fire that is a person’s mother and refuge, where they return and shelter.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r14.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: الهاوية النار هي أمه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها ويأوي إليها

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r15.speaker: الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r15.claim: Al-Ashʿath describes believing souls asking about the dead; when told one has died, they say he was taken to his mother, the abyss.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r15.anchor: عن الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى قال: إذا مات المؤمن ذهب بروحه إلى روح المؤمنين فتقول: روحوا لأخيكم

DURR-FULL:v8p605/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r16.claim: A report from the Prophet says a deceased person’s soul is questioned by believers; if dead, they say he went to his mother, the worst mother and nurse.
DURR-FULL:v8p605/r16.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا مات العبد تلقى روحه أرواح المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r13.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r13.claim: Many commentators say the mother is Hell itself, a level that shelters the unbeliever like a mother or the earth shelters people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r13.anchor: قال كثير من المفسرين: المراد بالأم نفس الهاوية، وهي درك من أدراك النار،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r14.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r14.claim: Others read mother as an ill omen, as in expressions about bereavement or a falling star.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r14.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو تفاؤل بشر فيه تجوز في أم الولاد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r15.speaker: أبو صالح وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r15.claim: Abu Salih and others say mother means his head, since the condemned fall headfirst.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r15.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وغيره: المراد أم رأسه لأنهم يهوون على رؤوسهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r16.speaker: طلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r16.claim: Talha reads fa-immuhu with kasra on hamza, ḍamma on mīm, and a doubled mīm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r16.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: «فإمه» بكسر الهمزة وضم الميم مشددة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r18.claim: A report says the Prophet explained his phrase la umma laka to mean that the man would have no fire, connecting the saying to this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r18.anchor: إنما أردت لا نار لك، قال الله تعالى: فأمه هاوية.

JISHUMI:v10p7519/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r10.claim: Hāwiya can describe rapid downward movement; Hell is named so because it plunges its inhabitants from its top to its bottom.
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r10.anchor: وسميت جهنم هاوية؛ لأنها تهوي بأهلها من أعلاها إلى أسفلها

JISHUMI:v10p7519/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r11.claim: Related Qur'anic expressions use hawā for moving toward something, being led astray, or falling; the word can also mean destruction.
JISHUMI:v10p7519/r11.anchor: ومنه: (استهوته الشياطين) أمالته إلى ما دعته إليه، ومنه: (والمؤتفكة أهوى)

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the abyss is Hell, called the person's mother because he will take refuge there as one takes refuge with his mother; a verse by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt supports the image, and the name also reflects falling into its deep pit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أن الهاوية جهنم , سماها أما له لأنه يأوي إليها كما يأوي إلى أمه , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r6.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r6.claim: Ikrima says the abyss is where the person's head falls into Hell; a poem illustrates that sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه أراد أم رأسه يهوي عليها في نار جهنم , قاله عكرمة .

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the lowly person's mother is Hell because he returns to it as a child returns to his mother.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r9.anchor: وسماها أما، لأنه يأوي إليها كما يأوي إلى أمه، قاله ابن زيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r10.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r10.claim: Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's verse calls the earth our refuge and mother, supporting the image of a place one returns to.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r10.anchor: فالأرض معقلنا وكانت أمنا فيها مقابرنا وفيها نولد

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r11.claim: Hell is called hawiya because its occupants fall into it despite the depth of its bottom; one report says al-Hawiya is its lowest gate.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r11.anchor: وسميت النار هاوية، لأنه يهوي فيها مع بعد قعرها. ويروى أن الهاوية اسم الباب الأسفل من النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r12.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r12.claim: Qatada explains fa-ummuhu hawiya as his destination being the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: معنى «فأمه هاوية» فمصيره إلى النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r13.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r13.claim: Ikrima says the person plunges into Hell headfirst.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r13.anchor: عكرمة: لأنه يهوي فيها على أم رأسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r14.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r14.claim: Al-Akhfash understands ummuhu as his stable abode, a meaning Qurtubi says is close to the others.

STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.claim: The final six verses contrast the recompense of those whose scales are heavy with good deeds and those whose scales are light.
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.anchor: The last six verses (vv. 6–11) contrast the recompense

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.claim: The light scales and abyss are linked to 7:9 and 23:103.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.anchor: For one whose scales are light, cf. 7:9; 23:103.

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r10.claim: “Mother” translates umm, from amma, to betake oneself or direct one's course; here evildoers direct themselves to Hell's abyss.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r10.anchor: Mother translates umm, which derives from the verb amma, meaning, “to betake oneself to” or “direct one’s course to.”

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r11.claim: This resembles verses about people wronging themselves and verses describing Hell or Fire as disbelievers' refuge.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r11.anchor: In this sense it is similar to verses that speak of those who wrong themselves

ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Meccan surah, probably revealed after At-Tin (surah 95).
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.anchor: An early Meccan surah, most probably revealed after surah 95 (At-Tin)

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:6-9:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:6-9:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:6-9:kommentar/r3.claim: The ambiguous threat that a person's mother is a chasm delays the clear Hell threat until verses 10-11 and closes the sura's central eschatological sequence.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:6-9:kommentar/r3.anchor: Sie fungiert aufgrund ihrer Mehrdeutigkeit als retardierendes Moment und geht erst im abschließenden Verspaar V. 10.11 in eine eindeutige Androhung der Höllenstrafe über

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.claim: The Meccan surah warns and gives glad tidings about resurrection, with warning as its dominant tone.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.anchor: بيان إنذار وتبشير بالقيامة يغلب فيه جانب الانذار، والسورة مكية

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r13.claim: Hawiya is Hell, named for the plunge of whoever is cast into it, a fall to the lowest depths.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r13.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بهاوية جهنم وتسميتها بهاوية لهوي من ألقي فيها

TABRISI:101:5-11/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:101:5-11/r6.claim: Hāwiyah means Hell, the sinner's resting place; in Arabic it can also be said of someone who falls into a terrible predicament.
TABRISI:101:5-11/r6.anchor: أي فمأواه جهنم ومسكنه النار وإنما سماها أمه

TABRISI:101:5-11/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
TABRISI:101:5-11/r7.claim: The sinner is called one whose mother is lost because he plunges headfirst into the Fire.
TABRISI:101:5-11/r7.anchor: إنما قال فأمه هاوية لأن العاصي يهوي إلى أم رأسه في النار

TABRISI:101:5-11/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:101:5-11/r8.claim: Another explanation says the person drops into an abyss whose depth cannot be reached.
TABRISI:101:5-11/r8.anchor: إنه يهوي فيها وهي المهواة لا يدرك قعرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r10.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r10.claim: Al-Layth says al-Hawiyah is a name for Hell and also a bottomless pit whose depth cannot be reached.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r10.anchor: قال الليث: الهاوية اسم من أسماء جهنم (¬6)، (والهاوية كل مهواة لا يدرك قعرها) (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r11.speaker: عطاء والكلبي وأكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r11.claim: Ata, al-Kalbi, and most commentators explain that the person's dwelling place is Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r11.anchor: (وهذا معنى قول عطاء (¬8)، والكلبي (¬9)، وأكثر المفسرين) (¬10)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r12.claim: Abu Ishaq says it is called his mother because a mother's home is the original place of rest; blazing fire replaces that refuge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r12.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وقيل لمسكنه "أمه"؛ لأن الأصل في السكون إلى الأمهات، فقيل الذي له بدل ما يسكن إليه: "نار حامية"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r13.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r13.claim: Al-Farra likens Hell to a mother sheltering her child: it is his mother because he has no other refuge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r13.anchor: الفراء: صارت هاوية مأواه، كما (تؤوي) (¬3) المرأة ابنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r14.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r14.claim: Muqatil says people head toward Hawiyah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r14.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول يؤم الناس (¬6) الهاوية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r15.claim: Al-Wahidi rejects that reading as an established interpretation because it requires pronouncing fa-ummuhu with fatḥa, a reading unreported from anyone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r15.anchor: وهذا إنما كان يحتمل لو قريء "فأمه" بفتح الهمزة، ولم يرو ذلك عن أحد.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r2.claim: One interpretation makes Hawiyah the person's destination and refuge, the abyss of Hell into whose shelter he is cast.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r2.anchor: varacağı yeri yatağı, kucağına sığınacağı ana vatanı hâviyedir.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r3.claim: Another reading takes the phrase as a curse or idiom: his mother will weep and collapse because he has perished.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r3.anchor: Diğer bir mâna ile o öyle sukūt edecektir ki anası ağlayıp yıkılacaktır.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r4.claim: A third reading makes the brain's root Hawiyah, or says the person falls headfirst to the bottom of Hell.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r4.anchor: Diğer bir mâna ile onun ümm-i dimağı, yani beyninin kökü hâviye olacak

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r7.speaker: Kāmûs
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r7.claim: The lexicon lists Hawiyah and al-Hawiyah among the names of Hell; the word derives from falling and can mean a deep, empty abyss.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r7.anchor: Kāmûs’ta هاوية ve الهاوية cehennemin isimlerindendir. Yukarıdan aşağıya düşmek

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r8.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r8.claim: Alusi reports that Hawiyah is so called because of its great depth; some restrict it to the lowest gate of Hell.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r8.anchor: Âlûsî’nin naklettiği vechile denilmiştir ki: “Ona hâviye ıtlak edilmesi gayet derin olmasındandır.”

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r9.claim: The term Hawiyah also occurs in translations of the Bible.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r10.claim: In the first interpretation, umm means a place of refuge by metaphor from a mother's lap, making the final refuge of the doomed painfully ironic.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r10.anchor: “me’vâ” ona teşbih edilmiştir ki bunda pek acıklı bir tehekküm vardır.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r11.claim: Arabs use hawat ummuhu as an indirect imprecation for someone's destruction, since a mother grieves and faints when her child dies; it can also express amazement or praise.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r11.anchor: Araplar bir kimsenin helâkine dua makāmında kinaye tarîkiyle هوت أمه derler

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r12.claim: Kaʿb ibn Saʿd al-Ghanawi and the Hamasa poet use the idiom in praise of brave dead warriors, not as a literal curse.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r12.anchor: şu beyti bu kabîlden olarak mâruftur:

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r13.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r13.claim: Qatada and many exegetes connect the phrase to the Arab idiom hawat ummuhu.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r13.anchor: Katâde’den bir rivayet olarak mervî olduğu üzere birçok müfessirîn

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r14.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf ve Râgıb
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r14.claim: Zamakhshari and Raghib prefer the idiomatic reading; Kashf's author calls it more eloquent for contrasting with the satisfied life, and Tibi calls it clearer.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r14.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf ve Müfredât’ta Râgıb bunu tercih eylemişler.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r15.claim: The idiomatic reading has a subtle force, but the refuge reading is clearer because the pronoun directly refers to Hawiyah and the metaphor intensifies the warning.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r15.anchor: evvelki mânada “hâviye”ye rücû‘u zâhir, istiare itibariyle mübalağa belâgati da şüphesiz olduğu için daha vâzıhtır.

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r16.speaker: Katâde, Ebû Sâlih, İkrime ve Kelbî
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r16.claim: They report umm as the brain or root of the head, with Hawiyah meaning Hell or the one who falls into it headfirst.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r16.anchor: Katâde’den ve Ebû Sâlih’ten ve İkrime ve Kelbî ve sâireden mervî olduğu üzere “ümm” “ümm-i dimağ” ve “ümm-i re’s”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.claim: Light deeds mean few or no good acts and imply sins outweighing them; the illustrative imagery teaches just judgment and responsible belief and conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.anchor: Amellerin hafif olması ise kulun dünyada yaptığı iyiliklerin azlığı veya bulunmaması demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.claim: Since afterlife events are unseen beyond what revelation states, one cannot speculate about how deeds will actually be weighed or measured.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.anchor: amellerin nasıl tartılacağı veya ölçüleceği hakkında söz söylemek yahut fikir yürütmek ise mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r6.claim: Umm literally means “mother” but metaphorically means shelter; the image is Hell eagerly opening its arms to sinners as a mother embraces her child.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r6.anchor: Burada mecaz olarak “barınak” mânasında kullanılmıştır. Âyette, annenin çocuğuna kucak açıp onu bağrına basmaya can attığı gibi cehennemin de suçlulara kucak açarak onları içine almak için iştiyakla beklediğini ifade eden kinayeli bir anlatım söz konusudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.claim: Those with few good deeds and many bad deeds go to Hell; commentators identify Hawiya as one of Hell's names.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.anchor: Tefsirlerde buradaki hâviye kelimesinin cehennemin isimlerinden biri olduğu belirtilmiştir

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p537#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p537#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p537#5/r1.claim: The Fire is his mother because he takes refuge in it as one returns to a mother.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p537#5/r1.anchor: هاوية} أي النار له كالأم يأوي إليها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r1.speaker: ابن خالد الوالبي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r1.claim: Ibn Khalid al-Walibi interprets ummihi as the crown or top of the head.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن خالد الوالبي فامه هاوية قال : أم راسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r2.claim: Ikrima says the person's head is falling into Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3458#4/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : أم راسه هاوية في جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r1.claim: Rāḍiya (content) is a transferred description of life: its possessor is content with it, or the life causes contentment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r1.anchor: ووصف الحياة ب { راضية } مجاز عقلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r2.claim: “His mother is an abyss” announces misery; it may literally use “mother” as a figurative equivalent of an person's condition, since Arabs associate a person's good or bad fortune with the mother's joy or grief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r2.anchor: والكلام تمثيل لحال من خفت موازينه يومئذ بحال الهالك في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r3.claim: The formula resembles “his mother perished” or “his mother bereaved him,” an inherited curse also used for wonder; Ibn ʿĀshūr analyzes a cited elegy as ellipsis and semantic abstraction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r4.claim: Alternatively, umm may be a metaphor for a person's place of refuge and destination, and hāwiya is a deadly low place between mountains, here identified with Hell or as its proper name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p514/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( أمه ) مستعارا لمقره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو صالح وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r1.claim: One interpretation says the person falls headfirst into Hell; ‘his mother’ means his head or brain, and Qatada and Abu Salih explicitly say they fall on their heads.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r1.anchor: فهو ساقط هاو بأم رأسه في نار جهنم. وعبر عنه بأمه-يعني (2) دماغه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r2.claim: Another view takes ‘his mother’ as his destination and return, with Hawiya itself a name of Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r2.anchor: فأمه} التي يرجع إليها، ويصير في المعاد إليها {هاوية} وهي اسم من أسماء النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says Hell is called his mother because he has no refuge besides it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r3.anchor: وإنما قيل: للهاوية أمه؛ لأنه لا مأوى له غيرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Fire is the person’s mother and refuge, citing that the Fire is their abode.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r4.anchor: الهاوية: النار، هي أمه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها ويأوي إليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r6.speaker: الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r6.claim: A report says a deceased believer’s soul joins believing souls, who ask about others and hear that one was taken to mother Hawiya; Ibn Mardawayh gives a longer marfu version from Anas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#3/r6.anchor: ذهب بروحه إلى أرواح المؤمنين، فيقولون: روحوا أخاكم، فإنه كان في غم الدنيا

KASHSHAF:101:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:9/r1.claim: The curse “his mother fell” is said over a doomed man: as he falls and perishes, his mother falls into bereavement and grief; the verse means the person whose scales are light has perished.
KASHSHAF:101:9/r1.anchor: من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة : هوت أمّه

KASHSHAF:101:9/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:9/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, Hāwiyah is a name for Hell, a deep fire into which its people plunge; a report says one falls in it for seventy years, so it is their abode.
KASHSHAF:101:9/r2.anchor: من أسماء النار ، وكأنها النار العميقة لهوي أهل النار فيها

KASHSHAF:101:9/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:9/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:9/r3.claim: The abode may be called a mother by analogy because a mother is a child's refuge and place of shelter.
KASHSHAF:101:9/r3.anchor: للمأوى : أمّ ، على التشبيه ؛ لأنّ الأمّ مأوى الولد

KASHSHAF:101:9/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF:101:9/r4.claim: Qatādah says the person's head, his “mother,” falls to the bottom of Hell because he is cast into it headfirst.
KASHSHAF:101:9/r4.anchor: فأمّ رأسه هاوية في قعر جهنم ؛ لأنه يطرح فيها

KASHSHAF:101:9/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:9/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:9/r5.claim: “It” may refer to the calamity implied by the first interpretation or to Hāwiyah; the final hāʾ is a pausal letter, which some drop in connected recitation while others retain, as in the written codex.
KASHSHAF:101:9/r5.anchor: والهاء للسكت ، وإذا وصل القارىء حذفها

MUJAHID:v2p778/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p778/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p778/r1.claim: Hasan transmits a Prophetic report that, when someone dies, his soul meets believing souls, who ask what became of a person; if told the person died earlier, they say he was taken to his mother Hāwiya, a wretched mother and nurse.
MUJAHID:v2p778/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مات العبد تلقى روحه أرواح المؤمنين فيقولون له ما فعل فلان

MUQATIL:101:9-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r1.claim: Hāwiyah is the person's origin or abode: earth will not carry him, the sky will not shade him, and only the Fire remains; he compares this usage with umm al-qurā, the origin of towns, meaning Mecca.
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r1.anchor: فذلك قوله: { فأمه هاوية } يعني أصله هاوية، كقوله: أم القرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#9/r1.claim: His mother means his dwelling and refuge, with the abode compared to a mother as a child's shelter and recourse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#9/r1.anchor: فمسكنه ومأواه النار وقيل للمأوى أم على التشبيه لأن الأم مأوى الولد ومفزعه

QUTB-ZILAL:101:9/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:101:9/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:101:9/r1.claim: As a child’s mother is its refuge, the people’s refuge and return on that Day is the Abyss; the elegant, partly obscure image prepares its later clarification and intensifies the effect.
QUTB-ZILAL:101:9/r1.anchor: والأم هي مرجع الطفل وملاذه . فمرجع القوم وملاذهم يومئذ هو الهاوية

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r1.claim: One view takes al-hāwiya as a name for deep Hell, into which its inhabitants plunge far; the phrase means that Hell is their refuge.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن الهاوية من أسماء النار وكأنها النار العميقة يهوى أهل النار فيها مهوى بعيدا ، والمعنى فمأواه النار

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r2.claim: A second view explains umm metaphorically as a refuge, like the mother to whom a frightened child runs.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r2.anchor: وقيل : للمأوى أم على سبيل التشبيه بالأم التي لا يقع الفزع من الولد إلا إليها

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r3.speaker: الأخفش، الكلبي، قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r3.claim: They interpret it as the head plunging into the Fire, since its inhabitants fall headfirst.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r3.anchor: ذكره الأخفش ، والكلبي ، وقتادة قال : لأنهم يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r4.claim: A third interpretation invokes the Arab curse hāwat ummuhu: when a man falls and perishes, his mother is imagined collapsing in grief, so the verse means he is ruined.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#4/r4.anchor: أنهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلاك قالوا : هوت أمه لأنه إذا هوى أي سقط وهلك فقد هوت أمه حزنا وثكلا ، فكأنه قيل : { وأما من خفت موازينه } فقد هلك

SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r1.claim: هاوية means doomed or destroyed and is a figurative expression: people say هوت أمه of someone who perished because his mother collapses in grief.
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r1.anchor: أي: هالكة، وهذا مثل. يقولون لمن هلك: " هوت أمه " لأنه إذا هلك سقطت أمه ثكلا وحزنا

SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r2.claim: A poet uses the idiom هوت أمه in a line about the morning traveler and the returning night.
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r2.anchor:
وعليه قول الشاعر:
4635- هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح غاديا

SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r3.speaker: طلحة
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r3.claim: Ṭalḥa reads فإمه with kasra on the hamza; Ibn Durayd, as transmitted by Ibn Khalawayh, identifies this as a dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r3.anchor: وقرأ طلحة " فإمه " بكسر الهمزة. نقل ابن خالويه عن ابن دريد أنها لغة

SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r4.speaker: النحويون
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r4.claim: Grammarians permit this kasra only when preceded by a kasra or yāʾ; the fuller discussion of the reading differences appears in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 4:11.
SAMIN-DURR:101:9/r4.anchor: والنحويون لا يجيزون ذلك إلا إذا تقدمها كسرة أو ياء. وقد تقدم تحقيق هذا في سورة النساء، واختلاف القراء فيه

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r1.claim: When a person’s good deeds weigh light, the Hawiyah is his refuge and abode: the Fire into which he falls headfirst.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأما من خفت موازينه فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] «وهي النار، هي مأواهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Hawiyah is the Fire, their abode.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {وأما من خفت موازينه فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] «وهي النار، هي مأواهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r3.claim: Qatāda says the destination is the Fire and explains hawat ummuhu as an Arabic phrase for falling into a severe predicament.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: هي كلمة عربية، كان الرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد، قال: هوت أمه

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r4.speaker: الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r4.claim: Al-Ashʿath describes believers’ spirits welcoming a dead brother from worldly distress; when asked about absent people, they are told some were taken to their mother, the Hawiyah.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r4.anchor: عن الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى، قال: " إذا مات المؤمن ذهب بروحه إلى أرواح المؤمنين، فيقولون: روحوا أخاكم

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says they fall into the Fire on their heads.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قوله {فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] قال: «يهوون في النار على رءوسهم»

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r6.claim: Qatāda says the person falls into the Fire headfirst.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] قال: «يهوي في النار على رأسه»

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Fire is his mother, abode, and return-place, citing the statement that their refuge is the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] قال: الهاوية: النار هي أمه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها، ويأوي إليها

TAB-FULL:v24p596/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Fire is made his mother because it is his only refuge, like a woman sheltering her child.
TAB-FULL:v24p596/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {فأمه هاوية} [القارعة: 9] «وهو مثلها، وإنما جعل النار أمه، لأنها صارت مأواه، كما تؤوي المرأة ابنها

WAHIDI-QT:101:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:101:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:101:9/r1.claim: The person whose scales are light has the Fire as his abode; his mother is the abyss.
WAHIDI-QT:101:9/r1.anchor: وأما من خفت موازينه } { فأمه هاوية } فمسكنه النار

ASAD-NOTES:101:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:1#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:1#n2/r1.claim: Literally, the sinner's “mother” or goal is an abyss of suffering and despair; umm idiomatically means what embraces or enfolds.
ASAD-NOTES:101:1#n2/r1.anchor: is used idiomatically to denote something that embraces or enfolds.

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Fischer
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r1.claim: Fischer reads the phrase idiomatically as a wish that one's mother fall, a euphemism for perishing.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Idiomatisch: „Seine Mutter stürzt“ = „Seine Mutter möge dem Fall preisgegeben sein“ – „eine Art Euphemismus für einfaches halaka ‚der geht zu Grunde’“ (so Fischer 1906, 41).

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r2.claim: The topological reading takes hawiya as a gorge or abyss, hence Hell; lexicographers support the equivalence with mahwa or mahwat.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Topologisch: „Seine Mutter ist ein Schlund, Abgrund“, wobei hāwiya ein Synonym für mahwā bzw. mahwāt

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Fischer
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r3.claim: Fischer prefers the idiom; the author acknowledges its supporting evidence but finds a purely idiomatic reading difficult because the next teaching question should refer to hawiya.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Zugunsten der von August Fischer präferierten Deutung des Verses im Sinne des Idioms hawat ʾummuhū spricht

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Fischer
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r4.claim: Fischer even treats verses 10–11 as a later addition to preserve the idiomatic reading; the author considers this an unsupported textual split.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Fischer geht deshalb sogar so weit, V. 10.11 für einen späteren Zusatz zu halten

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Paret
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r5.claim: Paret makes hiya refer nonspecifically to the preceding statement as a whole, but the author rejects this as inconsistent with the usual concrete referent and feminine pronoun.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Parets Übersetzung von V. 10 („Doch wie kannst du wissen, was das bedeutet?“) ist offensichtlich bemüht

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r6.claim: Dictionary equivalences between hawiya and mahwa or mahwat are not confined to explanations of this Quranic verse, supporting an independent lexical basis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r6.anchor: die Gleichsetzung von hāwiya mit mahwā bzw. mahwāt in den Wörterbüchern gerade nicht im Zusammenhang mit 101:9 behandelt wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r7.speaker: Sells
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r7.claim: Sells objects that early Arabic attestations for hawiya meaning abyss are tenuous; the author answers that lexicographical evidence and rhyme support the word.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r7.anchor: dass „attestations for the term hāwiya meaning abyss in early Arabic are tenuous“ (Sells 1993, 418), greift angesichts der lexikographischen Belege nicht

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r8.claim: The topological reading is reinforced by Hell as abyss in Revelation 9:1,11 and by Quranic teaching questions about obscure place names in 83:7–8 and 83:18–19; an intended echo of the idiom may coexist.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Die topologische Deutung von hāwiya wird überdies dadurch bestätigt, dass die Hölle auch in der Offenbarung des Johannes 9:1.11 als „Abgrund“ bezeichnet wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r9.claim: Some commentators gloss hawiya as a proper name for Hell, but this likely secondary interpretation entered the lexicons.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r9.anchor: manche islamische Kommentatoren hāwiya einfach als einen Eigennamen für die Hölle aufzufassen

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r10.speaker: Torrey
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r10.claim: Torrey derives hawiya from Hebrew howa, “destruction”; the author doubts early Meccan listeners knew a term found only twice in the Hebrew Bible.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r10.anchor: Torrey zufolge handelt es sich bei hāwiya um eine Arabisierung von hebr. hōwā, „Verderben“

CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r11.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r11.speaker: Bellamy
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r11.claim: Bellamy emends the consonantal text to fa-ummatun hāwiya, “a steep downward path”; the author notes no such variant is attested and calls it an easier secondary reading.
CORPUSCORANICUM:101:9:anmerkung/r11.anchor: Bellamy 1992 plädiert dafür, den rasm von V. 9 als fa-ʾummatun hāwiya („ein steiler Weg nach unten“) zu emendieren.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the one whose scales are light has his destination in the Fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فأمه هاوية ﴾ قال مصيره إلى النار

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r2.claim: Qatada says ‘hāwiya’ is an Arabic expression used of someone who falls into a severe calamity: ‘his mother has cast him down.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة هي كلمة عربية وكان الرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد قالوا هوت به أمه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r3.speaker: أشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r3.claim: Ash‘ath says a dead believer’s soul joins other believers, who ask about the living; when told someone has died but not arrived, they say he was taken to his mother, the Abyss.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#2/r3.anchor: عن أشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى قال إذا مات المؤمن ذهب بروحه إلى أرواح المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r1.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r1.claim: ‘Its mother’ means his refuge or abode, according to Ibn Zayd and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r1.anchor: ( فأمه ) أي فماواه كما قال ابن زيد وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r2.claim: Hāwiya means the Fire, as the following divine statement indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#3/r2.anchor: ( هاوية ) أريد بها النار كما يؤذن به قوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r8.claim: Ummuhu hawiya may curse that his mother fell in grief, meaning he is destroyed; another view names the deep fire where the damned fall.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r8.anchor: { فأمه هاوية } من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r9.claim: A report says the person falls into the Fire for seventy autumns, meaning his abode is the Fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r9.anchor: كما روي : ( 1336 ) ( يهوي فيها سبعين خريفا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r10.claim: “Mother” may figuratively mean one's refuge, since a mother shelters and comforts her child.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r11.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r11.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as the head plunging into Hell's depths because the person is thrown in upside down.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r11.anchor: وعن قتادة : فأمه هاوية ، أي : فأم رأسه هاوية

RAZI:101:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:101:3/r2.claim: The wording differs because the striking Event is perceptible, whereas the Abyss is not; therefore the verse asks what the Event is but not what the Abyss is.

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r1.claim: The description of Fire as the person's mother is a rational metaphor: it is his dwelling and return, as a child returns to its mother.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r1.anchor: فتوصيف النار بالهاوية مجاز عقلي كتوصيف العيشة بالراضية وعد هاوية أما للداخل فيها لكونها مأواه ومرجعه

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r2.claim: An alternative takes umm to mean the head: his head falls into Hell because people are thrown in headfirst.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بأمه ام رأسه والمعنى فام رأسه هاوية أي ساقطة فيها لأنهم يلقون في النار على ام رأسهم

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r3.claim: The head-first interpretation is unlikely because the pronoun in “what is it?” would then lack an apparent antecedent.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r3.anchor: ويبعده بقاء الضمير في قوله { ماهيه } بلا مرجع ظاهر

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r8.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r8.claim: Al-Qummi also says Hawiyah is his head, as he is cast into the Fire headfirst.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r8.anchor: وفي قوله { فأمه هاوية } قال ام رأسه، يقذف في النار على رأسه

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r9.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet says the gathered righteous ask a newly deceased believer about people who died before him; learning one was taken to Hawiyah, they lament the terrible mother and nurse.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r9.anchor: في الدر المنثور أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r10.speaker: أنس بن مالك والحسن والأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r10.claim: The author notes that the same meaning is also reported from Anas, al-Hasan, and al-Ashʿath al-Aʿma from the Prophet.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r10.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى عن أنس بن مالك وعن الحسن والأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r1.claim: The author rejects Christians’ biological reading of Jesus calling God Father; the Gospel uses father language for others too, so it admits a figurative reading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r1.anchor: ولو كان المسيح قال هذا في نفسه خاصة دون غيره، ما جاز لهم أن يتأولوه هذا التأويل في الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r2.claim: Father language for God means His mercy, generosity, and tenderness toward righteous servants, like a compassionate father toward his child.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r2.anchor: وتأويل هذا أنه في رحمته وبره وعطفه على عباده الصالحين، كالأب الرحيم لولده

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r3.claim: Jesus called water his father and bread his mother because bodies depend on them and the spirit survives through them, like children depend on parents for life and growth.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r3.anchor: وكذلك قال المسيح للماء: (هذا أبي) ، وللخبز: (هذا أمي) ، لأن قوام الأبدان بهما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r4.claim: Arabs called the earth mother because it is the origin of creation, the place of return, and the source of provisions and sufficiency.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r4.anchor: وكانت العرب تسمي الأرض أما، لأنها مبتدأ الخلق، وإليها مرجعهم، ومنها أقواتهم، وفيها كفايتهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r5.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r5.claim: Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s verse calls the earth our mother and refuge, illustrating the Arab usage.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r5.anchor:
وقال أمية بن أبي الصلت :
والأرض معقلنا وكانت أمنا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r6.claim: Hāwiya is the Fire, made the unbeliever’s mother because a mother shelters, feeds, houses, and raises her child, as the Fire does for the unbeliever.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p69/r6.anchor: لما كانت الأم كافلة الولد وغاذيته، ومأواه ومربيته، وكانت النار للكافر كذلك- جعلها أمه

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r1.claim: Hawiya is a level of Hell; umm here means a dwelling or refuge, as the earth is called humanity's mother because it houses people; Utba ibn Abi Sufyan uses the same image in battle.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r1.anchor: الهاوية دركة من دركات النار ، وأمه معناه مأواه

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r2.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r2.claim: Qatada, Abu Salih, and others say his head is in the abyss at the bottom of Hell because he is thrown in headfirst.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح وغيره : فأم رأسه هاوية في قعر جهنم

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an ill omen: people invoke destruction by saying “his mother fell,” since his fall and death make his mother fall into grief.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو تفاؤل بشر ، وإذا دعوا بالهلكة قالوا هوت أمه

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r4.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates the idiom with a line beginning “His mother fell”; the verse provides no poet attribution.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر : هوت أمه ما نبعث الصبح غاديا *** وماذا يرد الليل حين يؤون

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r5.speaker: الجمهور وطلحة
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r5.claim: Most readers pronounce the hamza of أُمُّهُ with ḍamma; Talha reads it with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { فأمه } بضم الهمزة ، وطلحة بكسرها

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r6.speaker: ابن خالويه وابن دريد
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r6.claim: Ibn Khalawayh reports Ibn Durayd's statement that the kasra is a dialect form.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r6.anchor: قال ابن خالويه : وحكى ابن دريد أنها لغة

ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r7.speaker: النحويون
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r7.claim: Grammarians say the hamza cannot be kasra unless preceded by a kasra or a yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:101:9/r7.anchor: وأما النحويون فإنهم يقولون : لا يجوز كسر الهمزة إلا أن يتقدمها كسرة أو ياء

ALUSI:101:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r1.claim: The passage summarizes the division of people into two groups and signals each group's particular state after describing what is common to all.
ALUSI:101:6/r1.anchor: بيان إجمالي لتحزب الناس حزبين وتنبيه على كيفية الأحوال الخاصة بكل منهما أثر بيان الأحوال الشاملة للكل

ALUSI:101:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r1.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
ALUSI:101:9/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd and others take ummuhu to mean his refuge or abode, and identify Hāwiya as the Fire.
ALUSI:101:9/r1.anchor: أي فماواه كما قال ابن زيد وغيره

ALUSI:101:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:9/r2.claim: The next verse's statement that it is a blazing fire explains Hāwiya after leaving it unspecified, heightening its strange and terrifying character.
ALUSI:101:9/r2.anchor: فإنه تقرير لها بعد إبهامها والإشعار بخروجها عن المعهود للتفخيم والتهويل

ALUSI:101:9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:9/r3.claim: It may be called Hāwiya because of the Fire's great depth and distance of descent; a report says its inhabitants fall into it for seventy years, and some specify its lowest gate.
ALUSI:101:9/r3.anchor: وذكر أن إطلاق ذلك عليها لغاية عمقها وبعد مهواها فقد روى أن أهل النار تهوى فيها سبعين خريفاً

ALUSI:101:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:9/r4.claim: Calling the abode a mother compares it to a mother's role as a child's refuge and is also a taunt; another comparison is the Fire enclosing the person like a womb.
ALUSI:101:9/r4.anchor: وعبر عن المأوى بالأم على التشبيه بها فالأم مفزع الولد ومأواه وفيه تهكم به

ALUSI:101:9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r5.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح وعكرمة والكلبي
ALUSI:101:9/r5.claim: Qatada, Abu Salih, Ikrima, al-Kalbi, and others understand it as his head's mother: his head plunges into Hell because he is thrown in headfirst.
ALUSI:101:9/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة وأبي صالح وعكرمة والكلبي وغيرهم المعنى فأم رأسه هاوية في قعر جهنم

ALUSI:101:9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:101:9/r6.claim: In another report, Qatada reads it as the Arab curse hawat ummuhu, wishing a man destruction: when he falls and dies, his mother falls into grief and sorrow.
ALUSI:101:9/r6.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن قتادة هو من قولهم إذا دعوا على الرجل بالهلكة هوت أمه

ALUSI:101:9/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r7.speaker: كعب بن سعد الغنوي
ALUSI:101:9/r7.claim: Kaʿb ibn Saʿd al-Ghanawi's verse is cited as evidence for the curse phrase hawat ummuhu.
ALUSI:101:9/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك قول كعب بن سعد الغنوي هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح غاديا

ALUSI:101:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r8.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI:101:9/r8.claim: Al-Kashf calls the imprecation reading best because it matches the emphatic wording of the preceding pleasurable life; al-Tibi calls it clearest, though al-Alusi leaves room for discussion.

ALUSI:101:9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:9/r9.claim: On the imprecation reading, hiya refers to the calamity implied by the discourse; in al-Alusi's reading it refers to Hāwiya, and on the head reading it evokes the understood fire.
ALUSI:101:9/r9.anchor: والضمير أعني هي عليه للداهية التي دل عليها الكلام وعلى ما قدمنا لهاوية وعلى الوجه الثاني لما يشعر به الكلام

BAGHAWI:101:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:101:9/r1.claim: His dwelling is the Fire; it is called a mother because people naturally settle with their mothers. Al-Hāwiya is a name for Hell and a bottomless pit.

BAGHAWI:101:9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:9/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI:101:9/r2.claim: Qatāda says hāwiya is an Arabic expression used of someone who has fallen into a grave difficulty: hawat ummuhu.

BAGHAWI:101:9/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:9/r3.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
BAGHAWI:101:9/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes ummuhu as the top of his head: they fall into the Fire headfirst.
BAGHAWI:101:9/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا التأويل ذهب قتادة وأبو صالح

BAYDAWI:101:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:9/r1.claim: His abode is the burning Fire, which is named al-Hāwiya.

BAYDAWI:101:9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:9/r2.claim: The following question, “what will make you know what it is,” points back to al-Hāwiya.
BAYDAWI:101:9/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال { وما أدراك ما هيه }

BIQAI:101:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:9/r1.claim: His “mother” is what shelters and embraces him; earth and a dwelling are called mother because one seeks and rests in them.

BIQAI:101:9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:9/r2.claim: The verse suggests he was created from Hell and dominated by a satanic, fiery nature.
BIQAI:101:9/r2.anchor: وهو يفهم أنه مخلوق منها غلب عليه طبع الشيطان لكون العنصر الناري أكثر أجزائه

BIQAI:101:9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:9/r3.claim: The indefinite description magnifies the place and indicates it offers no rest or stable ground.
BIQAI:101:9/r3.anchor: وعظمها بالتنكير والتعبير بالوصف المعلم بأنه لا قرار لها

BIQAI:101:9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:9/r4.claim: Al-Hāwiya is an extremely low, descending fire in which he keeps falling; the passage omits a hostile life in the second clause and a mother in the first.

BIQAI:102:1/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r1.claim: After al-Qāriʿa establishes the Hour, divides people into wretched and happy, and ends with the wretched, this sūra opens with the cause of misery to warn listeners away from it.
BIQAI:102:1/r1.anchor: لما أثبت في القارعة أمر الساعة

DURR:101:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:6/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:6/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:6/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:8/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:8/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:9/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:9/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:9/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r5.claim: Qatada says the person's final destination is the Fire, the Hāwiya.
DURR:101:9/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { فأمه هاوية } قال : مصيره إلى النار ، وهي الهاوية .

DURR:101:9/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:101:9/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as the idiom “hāwiyat ummuhu.”
DURR:101:9/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس { فأمه هاوية } كقولك هويت أمه .

DURR:101:9/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r7.claim: Qatada says Arabs use “hāwiyat ummuhu” when someone falls into a terrible predicament.
DURR:101:9/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قال : هي كلمة عربية ، إذا وقع رجل في أمر شديد قالوا : هويت أمه .

DURR:101:9/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r8.speaker: أبو خالد الوالبي
DURR:101:9/r8.claim: Abu Khalid al-Walibi interprets “his mother” as the top of his head.
DURR:101:9/r8.anchor: عن أبي خالد الوالبي { فأمه هاوية } قال : أم رأسه .

DURR:101:9/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:101:9/r9.claim: Ikrimah says his head falls into Hell.
DURR:101:9/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : أم رأسه هاوية في جهنم .

DURR:101:9/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:101:9/r10.claim: Abu Salih says they fall into the Fire on their heads.
DURR:101:9/r10.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال : يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم .

DURR:101:9/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR:101:9/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says Hāwiya is the Fire, the person's mother and refuge to which he returns and in which he takes shelter.
DURR:101:9/r11.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال : الهاوية : النار ، هي أمه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها ، ويأوي إليها .

DURR:101:9/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r12.speaker: الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
DURR:101:9/r12.claim: Al-Ashath says a believer's spirit joins the spirits of believers; they ask about the living, and wonder when a deceased has not joined them, saying he went to Hāwiya.
DURR:101:9/r12.anchor: عن الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى قال : إذا مات المؤمن ذهب بروحه إلى روح المؤمنين

DURR:101:9/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:101:9/r13.claim: The Prophet says a dead servant's spirit meets believers' spirits; when they hear another deceased has not arrived, they say he went to Hāwiya, a bad mother and nurse.
DURR:101:9/r13.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا مات العبد تلقى روحه أرواح المؤمنين

DURR:101:9/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:101:9/r14.claim: The Prophet says believers ask a newly arrived soul about living people and say the dead person who has not arrived was taken to Hāwiya; they later let the newcomer rest from worldly distress.
DURR:101:9/r14.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا مات المؤمن تلقته أرواح المؤمنين

DURR:101:9/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:101:9/r15.claim: The Prophet describes the believer's soul being welcomed by merciful souls like a bearer of good news; they ask about others and say a prior deceased went to Hāwiya.
DURR:101:9/r15.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «إن نفس المؤمن إذا قبضت تلقتها أهل الرحمة

DURR:101:9/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r16.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
DURR:101:9/r16.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak transmits Abu Ayyub's account of a soul welcomed by merciful believers; they inspect its deeds, rejoice at good, and pray over bad. Ibn al-Mubarak says Salam al-Tawil raised it from Thawr to the Prophet.
DURR:101:9/r16.anchor: وأخرج ابن المبارك عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال : إذا قبضت نفس العبد تلقاها أهل الرحمة من عباد الله

DURR:101:9/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:101:9/r17.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the dead receive news about their living relatives, becoming glad at good news and sad at bad; they ask whether a deceased has arrived.
DURR:101:9/r17.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قيل له : هل يأتي الأموات أخبار الأحياء ؟ قال : نعم ، ما من أحد له حميم

DURR:101:9/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r18.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR:101:9/r18.claim: In Wahb's story, Jesus questions a village whose people, jinn, animals, and birds died in punishment; they say their sins were serving false powers and loving worldly life.
DURR:101:9/r18.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه رضي الله عنه قال : مر عيسى عليه السلام بقرية قد مات أهلها

DURR:101:9/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r19.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR:101:9/r19.claim: Wahb's village story identifies Hāwiya as Sijjin, a vast fiery mass in which the souls were buried.
DURR:101:9/r19.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه رضي الله عنه قال : مر عيسى عليه السلام بقرية قد مات أهلها

DURR:101:9/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r20.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR:101:9/r20.claim: The village's respondent says the others cannot speak because they are muzzled with fiery bridles; he was caught in their punishment despite not sharing their condition and fears his fate.
DURR:101:9/r20.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه رضي الله عنه قال : مر عيسى عليه السلام بقرية قد مات أهلها

DURR:101:9/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r21.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
DURR:101:9/r21.claim: Jesus tells his companions that barley bread, plain water, and sleeping on dung among dogs are preferable when accompanied by well-being in this life and the next.
DURR:101:9/r21.anchor: فقال عيسى : وما الهاوية ؟ قال : سجين . قال : وما سجين ؟ قال : جمرة من نار

IBNASHUR:101:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r1.claim: The statement announces misery; on the literal-mother reading, Hawiyah means perishing and evokes a mother's intense joy or grief as a picture of the person's fate.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فأمه هاوية } إخبار عنه بالشقاء وسوء الحال ، فالأم هنا يجوز أن تكون مستعملة في حقيقتها . وهاوية : هالكة

IBNASHUR:101:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r2.claim: Arabs portray a person's state through the mother, who loves her child intensely; a Bedouin hearing that God took Abraham as a close friend exclaimed that Abraham's mother must be delighted.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r2.anchor: لأن العرب يكنون عن حال المرء بحال أمه في الخير والشر لشدة محبتها ابنها

IBNASHUR:101:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r3.claim: A Bedouin behind an imam heard the verse about God taking Abraham as a close friend and remarked that Abraham's mother must have been delighted.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r3.anchor: صلّى أعرابي وراءَ إمام فقرأ الإِمام : { واتخذ اللَّه إبراهيم خليلاً }

IBNASHUR:101:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r4.claim: The idiom هوت أمه is a curse wishing deadly harm, like ثكلته أمه; it can also express astonishment, as in Kaʿb ibn Saʿd al-Ghanawi's elegy.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r4.anchor: ويقولون في الشر : هَوتْ أمه ، أي أصابه ما تَهلك به أمه ، وهذا كقولهم : ثكلته أمه ، في الدعاء

IBNASHUR:101:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r5.claim: In the elegy, the object of what dawn brings and night returns is omitted but recoverable from context; مِن is understood in a detached construction, as in لقيت منه أسداً.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r5.anchor: وحذف منه في الموضعين اعتماداً على قرينة رفع الصبح والليل وذِكر : غادياً ويؤوب و ( مِن ) المقدَّرة تجريدية

IBNASHUR:101:9/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r6.claim: The verse reuses a fixed expression of destruction for a comparable fate, alluding to the comparison by means of the familiar idiom.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r6.anchor: فاستعمل المركب الذي يقال عند حال الهلاك وسوء المصير في الحالة المشبهة بحال الهلاك ، ورمز إلى التشبيه بذلك المركب

IBNASHUR:101:9/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r7.claim: Alternatively, أمه is a metaphor for one's resting place and destination, where one takes refuge as a child does with its mother.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون « أمه » مستعاراً لمقره ومآله لأنه يأوي إليه كما يأوي الطفل إلى أمه

IBNASHUR:101:9/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r8.claim: A hawiyah is a low place between mountains where a fall kills; here it means Hell, and some say it is Hell's proper name.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r8.anchor: و{ هاوية } المكان المنخفض بين الجبلين الذي إذا سقط فيه إنسان أو دابة هلك ، يقال : سقط في الهاوية

IBNASHUR:101:9/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r9.claim: Hawiyah is identified with Hell, so the phrase means that his refuge is Hell.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r9.anchor: وأريد بها جهنم ، وقيل : هي اسم لجهنم ، أي فمأواه جهنم

IBNASHUR:101:9/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:9/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:9/r10.claim: Alternatively, أمه abbreviates أم رأسه, the crown of the head, while هاوية means fallen, as in the idiom سقوط on one's crown meaning death.
IBNASHUR:101:9/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون « أمه » على حذف مضاف ، أي أم رأسه ، وهي أعلى الدماغ ، و { هاوية } ساقطة من قولهم سقط على أم رأسه

IBNATIYYA:101:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r1.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r1.claim: Many exegetes identify the mother as the abyss itself, a level of Hell; it is called the person’s mother because it shelters him, just as earth shelters people.
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r1.anchor: قال كثير من المفسرين : المراد بالأم نفس الهاوية ، وهي درك من أدراك النار ، وهذا كما يقال للأرض : أم الناس

IBNATIYYA:101:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r2.speaker: عتبة بن أبي سفيان
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r2.claim: ʿUtba ibn Abī Sufyān’s battle saying calls the earth the mother of its people, illustrating the sheltering sense behind the expression.
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r2.anchor: وكما قال عتبة بن أبي سفيان في الحرب : فنحن بنوها ، وهي أمنا

IBNATIYYA:101:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r3.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r3.claim: Others take it as ominous figurative speech, like saying someone’s mother is bereaved or his star has fallen.
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : هو تفاؤل بشر فيه تجوز

IBNATIYYA:101:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r4.speaker: أبو صالح وغيره
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r4.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ and others take “his mother” to mean his head, because the condemned fall headfirst.
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r4.anchor: وقال أبو صالح وغيره : المراد أم رأسه ؛ لأنهم يهوون على رؤوسهم

IBNATIYYA:101:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r5.speaker: طلحة
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r5.claim: Ṭalḥa reads fa-immuhu with kasra on the hamza and a doubled, ḍamma-marked mīm.
IBNATIYYA:101:9/r5.anchor: وقرأ طلحة : «فإمُّه » بكسر الهمزة وضم الميم المشددة

IBNKATHIR:101:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وأبو صالح، وقتادة
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the person falls headfirst into Hell, with umm here meaning the head or brain; Ibn Kathir reports this from Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, Abu Salih, and Qatada.
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r1.anchor: روي نحو هذا عن ابن عباس ، وعكرمة ، وأبي صالح ، وقتادة - قال قتادة : يهوي في النار على رأسه

IBNKATHIR:101:9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes his mother as the refuge to which he returns, with Hawiya being a name for Hell.
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r2.anchor: وقيل : معناه : { فَأُمُّهُ } التي يرجع إليها ، ويصير في المعاد إليها { هَاوِيَةٌ } وهي اسم من أسماء النار

IBNKATHIR:101:9/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir explains that Hell is called his mother because he has no refuge other than it.
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r3.anchor: قال ابن جرير : وإنما قيل للهاوية : أمه ؛ لأنه لا مأوى له غيرها

IBNKATHIR:101:9/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says Hawiya is Hell, the person's mother and refuge to which he returns; he cites the verse saying their abode is the Fire.
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : الهاوية : النار ، هي أمه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها ، ويأوي إليها ، وقرأ : { وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ }

IBNKATHIR:101:9/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r5.claim: A report from Qatada identifies Hawiya as the Fire and their abode.
IBNKATHIR:101:9/r5.anchor: قال ابن أبي حاتم : وروي عن قتادة أنه قال : هي النار ، وهي مأواهم

MAWARDI:101:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies Hawiya as Hell, called the person's mother because he takes refuge there as a child does with its mother; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poem supports the refuge sense.
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الهاوية جهنم ،   سماها أُمَّا له ؛ لأنه يأوي إليها كما يأوي إلى أُمّه ،   قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI:101:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.claim: Hell is called Hawiya because the person falls into it, though it has a deep abyss.
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.anchor: وسميت النار هاوية ؛ لأنه يهوى فيها مع بعد قعرها .

MAWARDI:101:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.claim: ʿIkrima instead reads mother as the person's own head, upon which he falls into Hell; a poem addressed to ʿAmr illustrates this image.
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.anchor:
الثاني : أنه أراد أُمّ رأسه يهوي عليها في نار جهنم ،   قاله عكرمة . وقال الشاعر :
يا عَمروُ لو نَالَتْك أَرْحامُنا

MAWARDI:101:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
